newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan ups nuke accident compensation to T$4.2 bln.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan ups nuke accident compensation to T$4.2 bln.

text.p: Taiwan's parliament has approved a sharp increase in compensation for nuclear disasters to up to T$4.2 billion (US$153 million) from T$70 million ($2.5 million), officials said on Friday.
The passage of the law was aimed to ensure economic growth and protect the public interests, the Economic Ministry said in a statement.
The ministry vows to strengthen supervision of nuclear facilities and to minimize possible risks.
The ministry statement defined nuclear disaster as any damage related to or caused by nuclear facilities. Only Taiwanese citizens would be eligible for compensation.
Taiwan has three nuclear power plants operating and a fourth under construction in northern Taipei county.
Since 1982, Taiwan has stored 97,572 barrels of nuclear waste at Lanyu, nearing its capacity of 98,112 barrels.
State utility Taiwan Power Company has promised to remove all the nuclear waste in Lanyu by 2000 and it has been seeking sites overseas, including China, Marshall Islands and Russia.

Taiwan has said it would press ahead with a controversial plan to ship up to 200,000 barrels of low-radiation nuclear waste to North Korea, despite pressure from South Korea and world environmental organisations.
South Korea, worried the deal could pollute the Korean peninsula with radioactivity, says there is no verification that the North -- Seoul's arch-rival -- can store the waste safely.
Taiwan maintains the Taipei-Pyongyang waste pact complies with all international regulations and that shipments would be securely packed in steel barrels.
Taiwan has no diplomatic ties with either North Korea or South Korea, both of which recognise Taiwan's own rival -- the communist Chinese government in Beijing. (US$1 = T$27.5)
